chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Fadl ibn Abdul Malik who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries off his son while he is young. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' I said: 'Is the father's divorce valid?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said: 'Upon whom is the dower?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon the father, if he guaranteed it for them, and if he did not guarantee it, then it is upon the boy, unless the boy has no wealth, in which case the father is responsible for it even if he did not guarantee it.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the man marries off his son, that is up to him (the son), and when he marries off his daughter, it is valid.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for marrying off a minor son or daughter in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between marrying a minor son versus a daughter, emphasizing the father's role as the legal guardian (wali) who bears financial responsibility for the son's dower unless otherwise specified. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that while the father's authority is sufficient for a daughter, the son's marriage involves specific conditions regarding the validity of divorce and the allocation of mahr based on the son's financial status. This ruling underscores the practical application of guardianship rights in early Islamic family law.
